notifications.message: The SW-CORE-1 device has an extended ACL named 'ALLOW_ALL' with the rule 'permit ip any any'. This rule, if applied, allows unrestricted IP traffic between all routed VLANs (VLAN 10 USERS, VLAN 20 SERVERS) and potentially to/from other networks. This completely negates network segmentation benefits, creates a significant security vulnerability, and directly violates the user's intent to implement secure inter-VLAN communication and deny specific services. All systems are exposed to each other.
notifications.title: Notification

notifications.message: SW-CORE-1's Gi0/1 interface is configured as a trunk, connecting to SW-ACCESS-1's Gi0/24. However, the discovery report indicates that SW-ACCESS-1 has no trunks configured (`trunks: []`). For VLAN 10 (USERS) traffic to be routed via SW-CORE-1, SW-ACCESS-1's Gi0/24 interface *must* also be configured as an 802.1Q trunk, explicitly allowing VLAN 10. If this interface is not a trunk, users in VLAN 10 on SW-ACCESS-1 will be unable to communicate with SW-CORE-1 and thus with other VLANs or the internet.
notifications.title: Notification

notifications.message: VLAN 30 (CAMERAS) is defined on SW-CORE-1, but no Switched Virtual Interface (SVI) or IP gateway is configured for it. According to the user intent, 'Cameras should be isolated'. Not having an SVI effectively isolates this VLAN at Layer 3, meaning devices in VLAN 30 cannot initiate communication with other VLANs. This configuration aligns with the stated goal of isolation, therefore it is not an immediate issue, but rather a confirmation of intent. However, any future need for communication (e.g., to a recording server, management platform) would require SVI creation and specific ACLs to maintain isolation while allowing controlled access.
